links.comparator_used: Baseline LLM prompt without empathy-oriented instruction
links.outcome: Affective polarity (extreme negativity), readability (FKGL grade level) and semantic fidelity to physician answers
links.effect: Reduced extreme negativity and lowered FKGL by up to 6.87 points for GPT-5; no significant increase in semantic fidelity
links.tradeoff: No gain in semantic fidelity to physician answers
links.quote: Empathy-oriented prompting reduces extreme negativity and lowers grade-level complexity (up to -6.87 FKGL points for GPT-5) but does not significantly increase semantic fidelity.

links.comparator_used: Original physician-authored answers and baseline LLM responses
links.outcome: Semantic similarity to physician answers, readability, affective extremity and patient preference
links.effect: Rephrase configurations reached semantic similarity up to mean = 0.93 and consistently improved readability and reduced affective extremity; patients consistently preferred rewritten variants for clarity and emotional tone
links.tradeoff: No model surpassed physicians on epistemic criteria in the dual stakeholder evaluation
links.quote: Rephrase configurations achieve the highest semantic similarity to physician answers (up to mean = 0.93) while consistently improving readability and reducing affective extremity.

design_hint: empathy-oriented prompting and collaborative rewriting of physician responses
